messages.subject: [R-wiki] How to upload a graphics file?
messages.subject_clean: [R-wiki] How to upload a graphics file?
messages.body_plain:
I was trying to upload a .svg file to the Wiki, but I couldn't see how 
to do it.

I clicked the "Add images or other files" button and got a page (with 
the category Mediafile Selection packages:cran), where I could browse to 
the file on my computer (mlgvswgt1.svg) and click "Upload".  However, 
even though it gave no error, there was no indication that the file was 
successfully uploaded, and I couldn't find it.  The 5 or 6 filenames and 
images in the right hand side of the "Add images..." window didn't change.

How do I go about uploading an image?

-- Tony Plate

messages.body_plain:
Hello Tony,

This is because the file format is not accepted. You should have a clear 
message in red telling that the "upload is denied because the file 
extension is not accepted" at the top of the upload page.

Here is the list of accepted extensions (file formats):

jpg     image/jpeg
jpeg    image/jpeg
gif     image/gif
png     image/png
tgz     application/octet-stream
tar     application/x-gtar
gz      application/octet-stream
zip     application/zip
pdf     application/pdf
txt     text/plain
html    text/html
htm     text/html
xml     text/xml
swf     application/x-shockwave-flash
r       application/r
rd      application/rd

plus a couple of other, less common ones. The .svg extension is not in 
this list because not all Web browsers support this extension. I suggest 
to convert your file into one of the supported formats. If you would 
like to keep it in vector format, convert it into .pdf or, better, .swf. 
Also, if you change the name of the file, do not forget to place the 
right extension at the end of the new name.
Best,

Philippe Grosjean

messages.body_plain:
Philippe, thanks, I guess I missed the error message the first time 
(small font, different part of the screen from where the "Upload" button 
is...)

I added a page to the wiki describing the RSVGTipsDevice package and I 
had wanted to include an SVG image precisely because of the special 
abilities of SVG -- pop-up tool-tips identifying points.  So, using 
another graphics format pretty much defeats the purpose.  But, I 
included an external link to the SVG image.

thanks anyway!

-- Tony
